This is a **template post**. Every folder in `projects/` with an `index.qmd` shows up on the Projects page. The chart below uses R's built-in `USArrests` data as a stand-in. Swap in your own analysis, such as the NPPES work.

```{r}
#| label: setup
#| message: false
#| warning: false
library(ggplot2)
source(here::here("R/theme_joydada.R"))
df <- data.frame(state = rownames(USArrests), USArrests)
```

## A chart in the site palette

```{r}
#| label: fig-bar
#| fig-cap: "Urban population share, top 12 states (USArrests, 1973)."
top <- head(df[order(-df$UrbanPop), ], 12)
p <- ggplot(top, aes(reorder(state, UrbanPop), UrbanPop)) +
  geom_col(fill = jd_pink[3], width = .7) +
  coord_flip() +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "Urban population (%)", title = "Most urban states, 1973") +
  theme_joydada()
ggsave("thumbnail.png", p, width = 6, height = 4, dpi = 150, bg = "white")
p
```

## An interactive map

```{r}
#| label: map
library(leaflet)
leaflet() |>
  addProviderTiles(providers$CartoDB.Positron) |>
  setView(-96, 38, zoom = 3) |>
  addCircleMarkers(lng = -75.16, lat = 39.95, radius = 8,
                   color = jd_pink[3], fillOpacity = .8, label = "Example point")
```

## Citing this post

Because `citation: true` is set in `projects/_metadata.yml`, Quarto adds a **Citation** section with BibTeX at the bottom of every project post. To get a DOI, connect the repo to Zenodo and cut a GitHub release.
